column3: rationale

The arm64 port establishes its original address-profile constants, topic 0012 replaces the platform split with one scalable Darwin profile, and topic 0032 retunes the auxiliary allowance so vmalloc address space stops being the binding constraint on vmapped kernel stacks.
The arm64 UML port owns its architecture capabilities while topic 0023 exposes ACK's architecture-gated Android system-mapping sealing policy.
The arm64 port owns mmap policy while topic 0012 rejects guest mappings that cross the shared sparse native hole.
The arm64 port owns its relax primitive while topic 0015 turns an interruptible Darwin spin wait into a safe cooperative IPI boundary.
The arm64 signal port owns its restorer while topic 0012 moves the trampoline with the selected guest task ceiling.

The shared port establishes UML build wiring, topic 0018 generates the arm64 kernel API headers required by ACK, and topic 0021 selects the freestanding arm64 Rust target for this Darwin-hosted kernel.
Topic 0010 introduces the Darwin user-network device while topic 0030 moves only its receive path onto NAPI so a sustained inbound stream cannot livelock the receiving CPU in interrupt context.
Topic 0010 adapts UBD host I/O to Darwin while topic 0033 corrects request advancement when one COW descriptor is split between backing and COW extents.
Darwin vhost-user transport support remains in topic 0010 while the generic 64-bit DMA-mask correction stays independently reviewable and droppable as topic 0011.
Topic 0010 owns the Darwin keyboard and absolute-pointer devices for every guest while topic 0029 reshapes only the pointer into the direct touchscreen Android's EventHub is able to classify.
The shared port establishes generic UML header selection while topic 0019 selects the generic SIMD-availability contract absent from ACK's UML headers.
The shared task-layout contract remains in topic 0001 while topic 0012 selects the common scalable Darwin guest unmapped base.
The shared port establishes UML topology while topic 0035 connects its immutable Darwin vCPU capacities to the generic scheduler scale.
The shared architecture contract owns kernel-side host helpers, topic 0024 adds the IRQ-enabled cooperative timer checkpoint, and topic 0026 generalizes its name for other safe in-kernel boundaries.
The shared host-service contract remains in topic 0001, topic 0028 adds the local IPI raise that arch_irq_work_raise() needs, and topic 0031 adds the host call that releases a reported free range.
The shared port establishes SMP declarations while topic 0035 adds the Darwin-only capacity and carrier-QoS profile contract.
The execution core owns Linux task entry while topic 0013 adapts its first activation to fixed Darwin vCPU carriers.
The shared SKAS bootstrap owns CPU0 setup while topic 0013 installs Darwin's signal stack on the new CPU0 carrier.

The MMU topic makes user-page lookup safe across sibling page-table changes, topic 0025 adds a non-atomic PREEMPT_NONE quiescent boundary after all lookup locks are released, and topic 0026 polls the cooperative timer before rescheduling there.

The SMP core owns the IPI vector table and dispatch, topic 0028 adds the irq-work vector and its arch_irq_work_raise() implementation, and topic 0035 atomically parses and installs Darwin vCPU scheduler capacities before domains are built.

The shared timer core owns Darwin timer delivery, topic 0024 exposes it through a kernel-register checkpoint for cooperative spin waits, and topic 0026 generalizes that checkpoint for safe retry and VMA-walk boundaries.

The MMU topic owns Darwin TLB synchronization and host invalidation, topic 0025 adds a quiescent boundary after each completed host VMA invalidation, and topic 0026 polls the cooperative timer there when logical IRQs are enabled.
The MMU core owns guest fault dispatch while topic 0012 rejects faults that intersect the shared sparse native hole.

The execution core owns Darwin task-size setup, topic 0012 selects the common Apple task ceiling and scalable native hole, and topic 0032 caps the auxiliary allowance and gives vmalloc the whole window rather than min(window, RAM).
The Darwin host implementation owns private service declarations, topic 0013 replaces per-task scheduler hooks with fixed-carrier lifetime hooks, and topic 0014 adds the host-stop boundary.
The Darwin host implementation owns the entrypoint while topic 0014 keeps last-ditch signals from running Linux cleanup on an arbitrary carrier task.
The Darwin host service implementation owns the physical-memory file while topic 0031 adds only the call that punches a reported free range out of it.
The Darwin host implementation owns logical IRQ state while topic 0013 documents and pins its fixed-vCPU carrier ownership.

The Darwin host implementation owns fault dispatch and scheduling; topic 0012 adds shared sparse guest-range validation, topic 0013 replaces per-task pthreads with stackful task contexts, and topic 0014 stops those carriers at safe guest or idle boundaries.

The Darwin host implementation owns SMP and IPI transport, topic 0013 turns each bootstrap pthread into its permanent named vCPU carrier, topics 0015, 0016, 0024, 0026, and 0028 preserve cooperative interrupt and timer service, and topic 0035 preflights and applies the capacity-matched QoS class when each permanent carrier is created.
The Darwin host implementation owns cooperative idle waits while topic 0014 adds the per-run stop descriptor to the wait set.
The Darwin bridge topic owns generated ABI declarations, topic 0012 carries the selected signal-restorer address, and topic 0014 adds the allocation-free active-stop event.
The Darwin bridge topic owns generated ABI identity while topics 0012 and 0014 advance it for the signal-restorer and host-stop contracts.
The Darwin bridge topic owns host-service declarations while topic 0014 exposes the per-run stop descriptor and predicate.
The Linux host implementation owns SMP and IPI transport while topic 0028 adds the local raise, which its queued self-directed signal already delivers correctly.
